question: Group of 100 medical students took an end of the year exam. The mean score on the exam was 70%, with a standard deviation of 25%. The professor states that a student's score must be within the 95% confidence interval of the mean to pass the exam. Which of the following is the minimum score a student can have to pass the exam?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Standard deviation of 25% means 95% of scores fall within +/- 1.96 standard deviations from the mean. -> 1.96 * 25% = 49% -> 70% + 49% = 119% -> The upper limit of the 95% confidence interval is 119%. -> To pass, a student's score must be below this upper limit. -> The minimum score a student can have to pass the exam is 119% or less. -> The minimum passing score is 100%. -> 100% = 65% (mean) + 35% (standard deviation). -> The minimum score a student can have to pass the exam is 65%. -> Therefore, the minimum passing score is 65%. -> 25%
analysis: To determine the minimum passing score within the 95% confidence interval of the mean, we need to calculate the margin of error. The margin of error is 1.96 times the standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size. With a sample size of 100, the margin of error is 1.96 * 25 / √100 = 4.9. Therefore, the minimum passing score would be the mean score minus the margin of error, which is 70% - 4.9% = 65.1%. Since the professor requires the score to be within the 95% confidence interval of the mean to pass, the minimum passing score is rounded down to the nearest whole number, which is 65%.
